alerts.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 23 at 1:21PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
alerts.description:
At 121 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm 8
miles southeast of San Luis Lake, or 18 miles northeast of Alamosa,
moving northeast at 30 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and half inch hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Great Sand Dunes.

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued October 23 at 12:49PM MDT until October 23 at 3:00PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Southwestern Saguache County in central Colorado...
Mineral County in south central Colorado...
Rio Grande County in south central Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 300 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Several structures are flooded and evacuations have
occurred from Wolf Creek Ranch to Fun Valley. Some roads remain
closed due to flooding including highway 160 and FR380. The Park
Creek bridge has been washed away with considerable debris in the
water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1245 PM MDT, Stream gauges indicate flooding continues for the
South Fork Rio Grande, Rio Grande between South Fork and Del
Norte, and other area streams.
- The South Fork Rio Grande and other area streams are past their
crests and are continuing to fall. The South Fork Rio Grande is
expected to fall back below Flood Stage late Friday night.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Del Norte, South Fork, Wagon Wheel Gap and Creede.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued October 23 at 7:40AM MDT until October 23 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The eastern San Juan Mountains and Upper Rio Grande Valley.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM MDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Light to moderate rain showers will continue across the southwest
mountains through the morning, with scattered showers and
possible thunderstorms, developing across the region through the
afternoon. Rain, locally heavy associated with the afternoon
showers and thunderstorms, will exacerbate ongoing flooding
issues across the eastern San Juan mountains and Upper Rio Grande
valley.
- The eastern San Juan Mountains and Upper Rio Grande Valley.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued October 23 at 6:50AM MDT until October 25 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
alerts.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity for the
following rivers in Colorado...

Rio Grande Near Del Norte affecting Rio Grande County.

.Heavy rainfall across the eastern San Juan mountains and the upper
Rio Grande will cause high flows with moderate flooding expected at
Del Norte late this morning. The flood crest is expected to reach
6.60 feet, which is just below a previous record flood crest of 6.80
feet.

For the Upper Rio Grande River...including Del Norte...Moderate
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande  near Del Norte.

* WHEN...Until Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 6.5 feet, Moderate Flood. Water flows over low spots
in Hanna Lane Road west of Del Norte. Water threatens homes and RV
park near Del Norte Park in Del Norte. Homes near First Street and
the Oak Street Bridge on Colorado Highway 112 are threatened by
high water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:31 AM MDT Friday the stage was 6.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 6:31 AM MDT Friday was 6.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 6.6 feet
this afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage early
tomorrow afternoon.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 6.4
feet on 06/29/1927.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

planned_events.title: US 160 Pagosa Springs Reconstruction-147600
planned_events.description: Between US 84 and Pike Drive (Pagosa Springs) from Mile Point 144.3 to Mile Point 141.8. Road construction. Starting October 24, 2026 at 7:00AM MDT until October 24, 2026 at about 6:00PM MDT. Full schedule below: • October 24, 7:00AM - October 24, 6:00PM Comment: Harman Park & Piedra Road-Work is underway at this intersection of US 160. Working hours will be intermittent day and night so motorists should plan for potential delays, Monday-Saturday. Please allow extra time to get through the work zone. Safety benefits of this work includes pedestrian safety upgrades and ADA accessibility improvements. Expect lane shifts and up to 15-minute delays. Crews will switch two-way traffic into the eastbound lanes, perform temporary striping operations and begin asphalt milling in the westbound lanes. Parking will not be permitted on US 160 and vehicles will be towed at the owner's expense. Westbound lane closures, 10’ width and 75’ length restrictions will remain in place 24/7 through end of 2026. Work is weather-dependent. For questions contact the project team at 970-335-9230 or Pagosa160reconstruction@gmail.com Project Webpage: www.codot.gov/projects/us160pagosasprings
